These dates describe this estate, not a regional rule or the invention of biodynamics.

claim:courbu-hondarrabi-zuri.statement: Plantgrape states that Courbu is officially designated Hondarrabi Zuri in Spain, while Gros Courbu is an official propagation-material alternative in France.

A later reselection of the parcels from which grapes may come cut the production potential from 4,800 to 3,200 hectares.

claim:crozes-hermitage-colours-grapes-17.statement: Crozes-Hermitage may be red or white. Reds require Syrah to be at least 85% of the encépagement, with Marsanne and Roussanne admitted as accessory varieties in mixed plantings up to 15% of the vines; whites are Marsanne and Roussanne.

It is the largest of the eight crus and the least uniform.

claim:crozes-hermitage-granite-crosses-r.statement: The Crozes-Hermitage specification identifies its northern granite as the same formation that appears across the Rhône around Tournon, in Saint-Joseph. Geology crosses the river and the appellation boundary; the law does not.

claim:crozes-hermitage-two-geologies-17.statement: The specification splits the appellation in two. In the north the Rhône has cut down to the granite de Tournon between Crozes-Hermitage and Serves-sur-Rhône, and sandy clays and granitic arenas are held on the slopes by dry-stone terraces. In the south and east lie Quaternary terraces of alpine gravels, with loess locally at the Gervans quartier of Les Blancs and distinctive kaolin sands at Larnage.

claim:crussol-limestone-17.statement: The Saint-Péray specification describes a primary-era granitic basement over which secondary deposits built a limestone massif, leaving the Crussol relief standing above the appellation, with soils that mix calcareous, clay-limestone and granitic material.

sources.publisher: Syndicat des Vignerons de l'AOC Condrieu
sources.title: Cave Yves Cuilleron — Condrieu

claim:cuilleron-scale-change-17.statement: The Condrieu growers' organisation records Yves Cuilleron taking over the family domaine in 1987 when it held 3.5 hectares in Condrieu and Saint-Joseph, and the estate reaching ninety hectares across six Northern Rhône AOCs plus IGP and Vin de France wines.

sources.title: An Interview with René-Jean Dard of Dard and Ribo

claim:dard-natural-wine-position-17.statement: Dard told Louis/Dressner that making natural wine "should not be a goal unto itself" but "a tool to make qualitatively superior wine", and that he had made sulfur-free wines since he was fifteen, following his father. He told LITTLEWINE that their goal is not to make wine without sulfites but to make good wine, and that if a wine is going a bit wild they do not stop themselves adding some.

claim:dard-ribo-cellar-17.statement: Reds are described as ten to fifteen days of maceration with whole bunches — unless sunburn requires sorting, in which case a destemmer is used — fermented in large wood with the cap broken once a day and aged in 500-litre demi-muids; whites are pressed whole-bunch.

claim:dard-ribo-farming-17.statement: Dard describes deciding to plough rather than use herbicides from the mid-1980s, and says explicitly that what interests them is "the notion of working cleanly" rather than holding an organic certification or a logo for the label. Absence of certification here is a stated choice, not evidence of conventional farming.

claim:dard-ribo-founding-17.statement: René-Jean Dard's own account gives 1983 as the first vintage he and François Ribo made together, and 1984 as the year they "began properly". CARTA keeps both: they are two different events, not one contested date.

claim:dard-ribo-tenure-17.statement: Dard describes the estate being assembled by renting vineyards from their owners and expanding gradually across parcels in Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage and Saint-Joseph. A single cellar point cannot stand in for that patchwork, and rented land is not owned land.

sources.title: Emmanuel Houillon and Pierre Overnoy profile

claim:emmanuel-overnoy-mentorship-12.statement: Louis/Dressner's profile and Emmanuel Houillon interview document Houillon beginning his apprenticeship with Pierre Overnoy in 1990, returning full-time in 1997, and taking over the estate in 2001 after years of working and learning alongside Overnoy.

claim:evangelho-site.statement: Evangelho Vineyard in Contra Costa County was planted in the 1890s on deep sandy soils; Soleras del Pacífico documents just over 100 Palomino vines there, while Bedrock identifies itself as the vineyard owner and farmer.

claim:fayolle-gervans-17.statement: Skurnik records a sixth-generation family estate at Gervans, Laurent Fayolle taking control in 2002 when his father and uncle divided the family domaine among their children, and seven hectares of parcels — many over sixty years old — in the granite hills behind the hill of Hermitage, across Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage and Saint-Péray.

claim:flor-evangelho-process.statement: The Flor of Evangelho is documented as a single-vineyard Palomino Fino wine in a fino-style solera established in 2017: native barrel fermentation is followed by light spring fortification to favor flor, fractional blending through a four-level solera, maturation under flor and unfiltered bottling.

sources.title: Jean Foillard — Côte du Py / Beaujolais context

claim:foillard-base-15.statement: Jean Foillard is shown at the official municipality point for Villié-Morgon because the verified producer material establishes the municipality but not a source-fit public cellar address.

sources.title: Jean Foillard — Côte du Py / Beaujolais context

claim:foillard-chauvet-influence-15.statement: Kermit Lynch describes Jean Foillard as following Jules Chauvet’s teachings; CARTA records INFLUENCED_BY and does not promote this to formal mentorship.

sources.title: Jean Foillard — Côte du Py / Beaujolais context

claim:foillard-producer-identity-15.statement: Jean Foillard is a Beaujolais producer based in Villié-Morgon whose documented wines include Morgon and Fleurie; CARTA keeps the producer identity separate from person:jean-foillard.

sources.title: Ordonnance du duc de Bourgogne Philippe le Hardi contre le Gamay, 1395
Philippe le Bon et la réglementation des vins étrangers à Beaune : enjeux économiques et politiques dans les ordonnances de 1466

claim:gamay-1395-ordinance-15.statement: A 1395 ordinance issued under Philip the Bold targeted Gamay in ducal Burgundy. CARTA records it as historical wine and economic regulation within its own territorial context, not as a modern Burgundy boundary statement.

sources.title: Historical Genetics: The Parentage of Chardonnay, Gamay, and Other Wine Grapes of Northeastern France

claim:gamay-parentage-15.statement: Microsatellite parentage analysis supports Gamay noir as an offspring of Pinot and Gouais blanc; Chardonnay is another offspring of the same parental pair, which does not imply stylistic equivalence.

sources.title: Jean Foillard — Côte du Py / Beaujolais context

claim:gang-of-four-beaujolais-community.statement: Kermit Lynch identifies Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Jean-Paul Thévenet as Beaujolais/Morgon producers who followed Jules Chauvet's methods and whom Lynch dubbed the 'Gang of Four'; his account credits their adoption of those methods with a dramatic change in Beaujolais wine quality and increased attention to the region.

claim:gilles-cellar-practice-17.statement: Rosenthal describes Gilles eschewing the destemmer in virtually all cases, working the vineyards by hand, using the grapes' own yeasts, ageing in old demi-muids and bottling without fining or filtration. These are concrete practices attributed to a producer, not a movement identity.

claim:gilles-marcel-juge-family.statement: Vine Trail identifies Cornas vigneron Marcel Juge as Guillaume Gilles's grandfather and describes Juge as an early personal reference point for Gilles's desire to work in wine.

claim:gilles-organic-current.statement: Vine Trail reports that Guillaume Gilles became certified organic from 2020 and describes hand vineyard work, whole-bunch red fermentation, native yeasts, no fining or filtration, and restrained sulfur use.

claim:gilles-producer-identity.statement: Guillaume Gilles is an independent vigneron based in Cornas; specialist sources document his own domaine from 2007 and the Cornas producer association lists him at 1 Grande Rue, Cornas.

claim:gilles-robert-michel-mentorship.statement: Robert Michel mentored Guillaume Gilles; Vine Trail says Michel offered Gilles an apprenticeship in 2000 and that Gilles worked with him until Michel's 2006 retirement, while Rosenthal explicitly calls Gilles Michel's protégé.

claim:gonon-farming-cellar-17.statement: The brothers are described as working organically, ploughing the steep slopes by horse, replanting by sélection massale from their own old vines, fermenting reds up to three weeks whole-cluster in open wooden vats and ageing in old 600-litre foudres.

claim:gonon-mauves-core-17.statement: The Rare Wine Co. places Gonon, with Gripa and Chave, among the last old-school Saint-Joseph growers based in the original appellation around Tournon, Mauves and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, records the brothers buying Raymond Trollat's 1915 planting on his retirement, and describes Marsanne planted by their father at the Coteau des Oliviers in 1958 and Roussanne in 1974.

claim:graillot-founding-succession-17.statement: Skurnik records Alain Graillot returning home to Crozes-Hermitage to start his own domaine in 1985, and his sons Maxime and Antoine being in charge since 2008, with hand harvesting, organic farming, whole-cluster fermentation and ageing in one- to three-year-old barrels bought from Burgundy estates.

claim:grand-cour-base-15.statement: Domaine de la Grand’Cour publishes its production base at 156 route de la Grand’Cour, Fleurie; CARTA geocodes that address as a point and does not use it as vineyard geometry.

claim:grand-cour-carbonic-practice-15.statement: Domaine de la Grand’Cour describes hand-harvested whole bunches placed uncrushed and undestemmed into low-temperature tanks saturated with carbon dioxide, followed by spontaneous fermentation to pressing without added sulfite or oenological products except intervention if a problem occurs.

claim:grand-cour-history-sites-15.statement: Domaine de la Grand’Cour states that Jean Dutraive acquired the estate in 1969 with nine hectares in Fleurie across Grand’Cour, Chapelle des Bois and Champagne; Jean-Louis Dutraive joined in 1977 and succeeded him in 1989.

claim:gripa-two-appellations-17.statement: The Guide Hachette records the Gripa family arriving at Saint-Péray in the seventeenth century and settling at Mauves around 1850, Fabrice Gripa running the domaine since 2001 after his father Bernard, and eighteen hectares spanning Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray with the Les Figuiers, Les Pins and Le Berceau cuvées.

claim:gros-manseng-origin-traits.statement: Plantgrape identifies Gros Manseng as originating in Pyrenean vineyards; it is vigorous and fertile, sensitive to powdery mildew, and relatively resistant to grey rot, with fruit able to remain on the vine for sweet-wine production.

claim:guigal-house-structure-17.statement: Maison Guigal records its founding by Etienne Guigal at Ampuis in 1946, Marcel Guigal taking over management in 1961 when his father lost his sight, Philippe Guigal joining as winemaker in 1997, a run of acquisitions including Vidal-Fleury, Château d'Ampuis, Jean-Louis Grippat, de Vallouit and Domaine de Bonserine, and its own cooperage from 2003. Scale, négoce and acquisition are part of this corridor's real ecology.

claim:jaboulet-ownership-transition-17.statement: The house records its founding in 1834 by Antoine Jaboulet on the hill of l'Hermitage at Tain, the creation of Hermitage La Chapelle in 1961, Gérard Jaboulet taking up the torch from 1977 until his death in 1997, and Caroline Frey assuming control in 2006 and beginning the conversion to organic and biodynamic farming. A historic house identity survived a change of owning family.

claim:jamet-parcel-mosaic-17.statement: The Rare Wine Co. records the Jamet brothers taking charge of the family domaine when their father Joseph retired in the mid-1980s, farming twenty-five plots across seventeen lieux-dits, and choosing each year which of those sites enter the flagship wine, with mostly whole-cluster fermentation and about 20% new wood.

claim:jurancon-2025-foothill-ripening-06.statement: Jurançon’s wet Atlantic foothills are tempered in autumn by a frequent warm, dry southerly foehn. On steep slopes and terraces, late, thick-skinned local grapes can concentrate while retaining high acidity and resisting grey rot, which helps explain how dry, sweet and late-harvest wines remain distinct paths rather than different places.

Successive picking passes are required except for Jurançon sec, while vendanges tardives fruit cannot be harvested before 2 November; off-vine passerillage is prohibited apart from handling within the parcel during harvest.

claim:landron-base-17.statement: Domaines Landron publishes its base at 3 impasse du Fief du Breil in La Haie-Fouassière; the Atlas point represents that base, not vineyard parcels.

claim:landron-history-17.statement: Domaines Landron records Jo Landron joining his father in 1979, abandoning herbicides and returning to soil cultivation in 1987, beginning organic conversion in 1999, receiving Ecocert certification in 2002 and entering Biodyvin certification in 2011.

claim:lapierre-base-15.statement: Domaine Marcel Lapierre is shown at its first-party address, 588 rue Rabelais, Villié-Morgon; the point represents the domaine base, not its Morgon or Beaujolais vineyard parcels.

assemblage-des-raisins.definition: Assembling permitted varieties as grapes, in the same proportion, rather than blending finished wines — the wording four Northern Rhône specifications use.
assemblage-des-raisins.matters: It governs when the varieties may meet. It never says whether a producer used the second variety at all.

carbonic-maceration.definition: A process beginning with intact whole bunches in a closed, oxygen-excluding carbon-dioxide atmosphere, with intracellular metabolism before pressing and fermentation completion.
carbonic-maceration.matters: It is a mechanism, not an appellation rule or a complete cellar recipe.

elevage.definition: The raising of a wine between fermentation and bottling: time, vessel, topping and other cellar choices all live inside it.
elevage.matters: Here it separates time in barrel from bottle age.

encepagement.definition: The variety mix planted across a holding, which is what the Northern Rhône's percentage rules actually govern.
encepagement.matters: An 80% or 90% Syrah floor describes the vineyard's planting, not the proportion of varieties in a finished bottle.

flor.definition: A film-forming yeast layer that develops on a wine's surface under the right cellar conditions.
flor.matters: It can shape aroma and structure more strongly than the grape name does.

foehn.definition: A warm, dry downslope wind. In Jurançon it can interrupt the wet Atlantic pattern during the long autumn ripening season.
foehn.matters: It helps explain concentration and drying conditions without pretending the foothills are generally arid.

igp.definition: Indication géographique protégée — a legal origin category broader than an appellation d'origine contrôlée.
igp.matters: A wine's category tells you which rules it met, not how good the site is: Seyssuel's slopes sit among the crus and its wines are IGP.

marl.definition: A clay-rich calcareous rock or sediment; Jura growers often distinguish its bands, ages and colors.
marl.matters: It is useful site context, not a flavor guarantee.

methode-traditionnelle.definition: A second fermentation carried out in the bottle the wine is sold in.
methode-traditionnelle.matters: It is a method. It is not a quality claim, and in this corridor only one appellation's specification covers it.

mistelle.definition: A sweet wine made by adding spirit to grape must before or during early fermentation.
mistelle.matters: Macvin belongs to this family; it is not another name for vin jaune.

nouveau.definition: A regulated early-release mention—also called primeur—currently available to qualifying red and rosé Beaujolais, not white.
nouveau.matters: It shaped global recognition without ever accounting for all Beaujolais production.

ouille.definition: Topped up: the barrel is refilled as wine evaporates, keeping headspace and oxygen contact low.
ouille.matters: It is the most useful word for avoiding the idea that every Jura white is oxidative.

passerillage.definition: Concentration as grapes lose water and shrivel, usually while remaining on the vine in this Jurançon context.
passerillage.matters: It is a ripening and concentration path, not another word for botrytis.

sec.definition: Dry. In this appellation the word is part of the legal name Jurançon sec and corresponds to a maximum fermentable-sugar threshold.
sec.matters: A bottle labeled only Jurançon is not the dry category.

semi-carbonic.definition: A related process in which ordinary fermentation of released juice can create carbon dioxide around intact berries in a whole-bunch vat.
semi-carbonic.matters: It does not require the same deliberately established external-CO₂ atmosphere as full carbonic maceration.

sous-voile.definition: Under a yeast veil: wine ages without regular topping while a film-forming yeast layer develops on its surface.
sous-voile.matters: This is biological ageing, not simple neglect and not a grape flavor.

tries-successives.definition: Successive picking passes through the vineyard, selecting fruit as it reaches the intended maturity or concentration.
tries-successives.matters: The current rule requires this repeated selection for Jurançon other than the sec path.

vendanges-tardives.definition: Late harvest, used here as a regulated Jurançon mention with its own grape, harvest-date and sugar requirements.
vendanges-tardives.matters: It is a narrower legal path than simply harvesting ripe fruit late.

vin-de-paille.definition: A wine from grapes dried after harvest; at Hermitage a governed optional mention requiring at least 45 days of drying, 170 g/L of natural sugar and a 15 hl/ha yield.
vin-de-paille.matters: It is a mention inside one specification, not a separate appellation and not a general regional style.

voile.definition: Literally ‘veil’: the film of yeast that can form over wine in a partly filled vessel.
voile.matters: The veil creates a biological pathway distinct from ordinary oxygen exposure.

whole-cluster.definition: Fermentation that includes intact bunches and stems.
whole-cluster.matters: Whole cluster describes grape handling; it does not prove that a ferment is carbonic or semi-carbonic.

Granite continues south while colour, grapes and wine forms change completely.

appellation:cornas.thesis: Cornas admits no accessory or white variety at all — the single-variety outlier among eight rulebooks. It is also where the corridor's sharpest legal trap sits: the appellation is delimited *within* a commune, so being in Cornas is not being Cornas.

featured_connections.reason: The rule governs when two varieties may meet, not whether any producer used the second one.
Half a hectare on the Côte Brune, at the opposite end of the appellation from a seventeen-lieu-dit mosaic.
A house founded in 1946 that has since acquired several of its neighbours is part of this appellation's real ecology.

appellation:cote-rotie.hero_kicker: Red only · and one white grape allowed in
appellation:cote-rotie.thesis: Syrah must be at least 80% of the {{term:encepagement|holding's planting}}, and Viognier may join it up to 20% of the vines — but only {{term:assemblage-des-raisins|assembled as grapes}}. A permission is not a practice: many Côte-Rôtie wines contain no Viognier at all.

featured_connections.reason: Old-vine Syrah from the flats in the commune of Cornas, bottled under this broader appellation.

appellation:cotes-du-rhone.hero_kicker: The valley-long background the crus sit inside
appellation:cotes-du-rhone.thesis: Côtes du Rhône runs from the Vienne sector towards Avignon and overlaps the northern corridor. In this world its job is to explain how a vineyard can sit among the crus and still be sold under a broader name.

featured_connections.reason: The lowest and youngest terrace, a triangle with its apex at Pont-de-l'Isère — a landform, not a delimited area.
Gervans is granite hill country behind Hermitage, and it carries the same appellation name as the gravel plain.
The commune named Crozes-Hermitage holds land in both appellations.

appellation:crozes-hermitage.hero_kicker: Eleven communes · granite north · gravel terraces south
appellation:crozes-hermitage.thesis: The largest cru is the least uniform, and its own specification says so: granite de Tournon on northern slopes, Quaternary alpine terraces to the south and east, loess at Gervans and kaolin at Larnage. It is not blank space around a famous hill.

featured_connections.reason: A governed mention with exact drying, richness and yield rules — not a separate appellation.
A domaine that rebuilds one blend from several sites each year, against a house that bottles named parcels.
The landform is one object; the appellation is another; the named sites growers talk about are a third.

appellation:hermitage.hero_kicker: One hill · three communes · three ways of organising it
appellation:hermitage.thesis: Hermitage is red, white and — under a governed mention — {{term:vin-de-paille|vin de paille}}. Its three communes include one called Crozes-Hermitage, which is the cleanest demonstration in the corridor that a commune name cannot tell you which wine a parcel may make.

featured_connections.reason: A producer based at Arlebosc in the Ardèche, outside this appellation entirely, whose vines and wines include Saint-Joseph.
Mauves, Tournon and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols are the 1956 heart of the appellation, and one cluster among several.
The granite of northern Crozes-Hermitage is the same formation exposed here at Tournon.

appellation:saint-joseph.thesis: Saint-Joseph is a corridor, not a côte. Created in 1956 on six communes around Tournon, expanded in 1969 by twenty more, then cut back by parcel revisions in 1994 and 2018 from about 6,800 to about 3,400 hectares. Today's outline is a made thing; the slopes did not move.

featured_connections.reason: One estate holds a traditional-method sparkling wine and a barrel-vinified still cuvée created in 1984, when most Saint-Péray was still sparkling.
The specification traces the sparkling reputation to trials on a hundred barrels in 1828, not to the 1829 date trade accounts prefer.
The corridor's cleanest legal contrast happens across a boundary the rock does not notice.

appellation:saint-peray.hero_kicker: White only · still and sparkling · next to Syrah-only Cornas
appellation:saint-peray.thesis: Two neighbouring appellations share a granite basement. One is red Syrah and nothing else; the other is white Marsanne and Roussanne and may sparkle by {{term:methode-traditionnelle|second fermentation in bottle}}. Nothing in the ground explains that.

appellation:savennieres.hero_kicker: One slope system · three legal identities · Chenin
appellation:savennieres.thesis: Savennières is read beside Roche aux Moines and Coulée de Serrant without merging their regulatory shapes or making the Joly estate the whole appellation.

featured_connections.reason: A white-only cru whose ground is more mixed than the Cornas granite immediately north of it.

geographic_feature:montagne-de-crussol.hero_kicker: Limestone left standing above a granite basement

featured_connections.reason: Morgon is the regulatory area around Villié-Morgon and Py hill—not a synonym for Côte du Py.

featured_connections.reason: The corridor is the only thing the eight crus share, and it is not a legal object.

The same four grapes travel a short distance and enter radically different physical, legal and human worlds — and the corridor itself has no legal boundary at all.

Blending two finished wines is a different operation, and the rule does not govern it.

practice:ouillage.thesis: {{term:ouille|Ouillé}} means topped up. In Jura it is the word that keeps grape identity from being confused with an oxidative cellar path.

practice:semi-carbonic-maceration.hero_kicker: Related to carbonic · not a synonym
practice:semi-carbonic-maceration.thesis: In a whole-bunch vat, ordinary fermentation of released juice can generate CO₂ around intact berries. That mixed mechanism differs from a fully established external-CO₂ treatment, and a regional tradition does not make it a universal legal requirement.

practice:sous-voile-aging.thesis: {{term:sous-voile|Sous voile}} is a biological ageing pathway under a yeast veil. It is not shorthand for every Jura white—or for simple oxidation.

practice:traditional-method-sparkling.hero_kicker: A method · not a quality claim
practice:traditional-method-sparkling.thesis: A second fermentation carried out in the bottle the wine is sold in. In this corridor it matters because {{term:methode-traditionnelle|it}} is what makes Saint-Péray the only cru whose specification covers sparkling wine.

practice:whole-cluster-fermentation.hero_kicker: A handling choice · not a complete fermentation diagnosis
practice:whole-cluster-fermentation.thesis: Whole cluster means intact bunches and stems enter the fermenter. To call the process carbonic or semi-carbonic, you still need evidence about atmosphere and fermentation—not a guess from the stem decision.

then.text: Eight generations culminated publicly in the Foucault brothers before the 2017 acquisition.

then_now.title: Continuity is not unchanged ownership

producer:clos-rougeard.thesis: Clos Rougeard links Cabernet Franc and Chenin to a long Foucault history, then marks a 2017 acquisition. Domaine du Collier is a family/work branch, not the same producer after succession.

producer:clos-uroulat.thesis: Clos Uroulat’s current visitor range makes a useful correction: Jurançon can be read across dry, tender and sweet positions instead of as a single binary switch.

producer:coulee-de-serrant.thesis: La Coulée de Serrant connects Chenin, a specific legal origin, a dated biodynamic conversion and the 2001 organization. Atlas keeps producer, appellation, advocacy and attributed philosophy as four different objects.

featured_connections.reason: Parcels here, in Hermitage and in Saint-Joseph, most of them rented rather than owned.
Whole bunches normally — and a destemmer when sunburn requires sorting.
Making natural wine “should not be a goal unto itself”, and sulfur goes in when a wine needs it.

producer:dard-et-ribo.hero_kicker: Mercurol · rented parcels across three appellations
producer:dard-et-ribo.thesis: A first vintage in 1983 and a “proper” beginning in 1984; a holding assembled by renting from owners; ploughing instead of herbicides from the mid-1980s and a deliberate refusal of certification as a logo. One cellar point could never stand for that graph.

featured_connections.reason: Alpine gravels on the lowest terrace, and nothing about flavour follows from that.
One name covering a gravel plain and a granite hill.

producer:domaine-alain-graillot.hero_kicker: Crozes-Hermitage · the terrace world made memorable
producer:domaine-alain-graillot.thesis: Alain Graillot came home to start his own domaine in 1985; his sons Maxime and Antoine have been in charge since 2008. He is why the flat southern half of the largest cru reads as a place rather than as leftover ground.

featured_connections.reason: White only, still and sparkling, immediately south of a cru that is red only.
Precursor of barrel work in Saint-Péray — not the inventor of still Saint-Péray, which already existed in tank.
The trials the specification treats as the origin of the appellation's sparkling reputation.

producer:domaine-alain-voge.hero_kicker: Saint-Péray and Cornas · both of an appellation's wine forms
producer:domaine-alain-voge.thesis: Les Bulles d'Alain is 100% Marsanne, {{term:methode-traditionnelle|méthode traditionnelle}}, four years on lattes, presented as continuing the tradition that made the region's reputation from the 1830s. Ongrie, created in 1984, is the same grape in oak when most Saint-Péray was still sparkling and still wines were made in tank.

producer:domaine-alexandre-bain.hero_kicker: Pouilly · a control dispute, not a tasting legend

then_now.intro: The claim is limited to the documented habilitation period.

now.label: MAY 2017 · remedy
now.text: The Dijon administrative court restored Bain's AOC rights.

then.label: SEPTEMBER 2015 · withdrawal
then.text: INAO withdrew habilitation on the stated basis of a required-control dispute.

then_now.title: Two dates replace one viral myth

producer:domaine-alexandre-bain.thesis: Bain's 2015–17 case establishes a mandatory-control dispute and a court remedy. Farming philosophy may be relevant producer context, but it is not the proven legal cause and later classifications require separate wine/vintage evidence.

featured_connections.reason: A recovery told through several growers instead of one.

producer:domaine-andre-perret.hero_kicker: Chavanay · the generation after the rescue
producer:domaine-andre-perret.thesis: André Perret returned to plant vines and develop the Condrieu AOC in the 1980s, with a first estate vintage in 1983 and thirteen hectares today, of which 5.5 in Condrieu. He is the reason the recovery is not a single biography.

featured_connections.reason: A founding story the corridor has never resolved, preserved rather than tidied.
Century-old vines from Verset entered this domaine's palette of sites.

producer:domaine-auguste-clape.thesis: Credited by one importer as the village's first producer to bottle his own wine in 1957 — while the specification dates the first bottling for a private cellar to 1952 and another importer credits Joseph Michel in 1956. Three accounts, all kept.

featured_connections.reason: A Saint-Joseph family holding a stake in the corridor's white-only cru.

producer:domaine-bernard-gripa.hero_kicker: Mauves · one family across a red cru and a white one
producer:domaine-bernard-gripa.thesis: A family recorded at Saint-Péray in the seventeenth century and at Mauves from around 1850, with Fabrice Gripa running the domaine since 2001 after his father Bernard, across Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray. CARTA carries this at reference-guide fitness and says so.

producer:domaine-cauhape.hero_kicker: Monein · slope, altitude and stylistic range
producer:domaine-cauhape.thesis: Domaine Cauhapé is a scale-and-range anchor: southeast-facing Monein slopes rising toward 400 metres, with dry and sweet wines held in the same estate frame.

featured_connections.reason: Twenty-five plots across seventeen lieux-dits under the same appellation name.
One legal origin holding a micro-estate and a house that has bought its neighbours.
Sérine is a local selection and naming habit attached to Syrah, not a second grape identity.

producer:domaine-christiane-chambeyron-m.hero_kicker: Ampuis · half a hectare on the Côte Brune
producer:domaine-christiane-chambeyron-m.thesis: Teaching value is not proportional to fame or hectares. One parcel, one grape, one current steward and an unusually exact cellar sequence make the difference between a locality and a parcel polygon impossible to ignore.

producer:domaine-de-la-grand-cour.hero_kicker: Fleurie · named sites and an explicit CO₂ protocol
producer:domaine-de-la-grand-cour.thesis: Grand’Cour makes producer specificity do the teaching: a Fleurie history across named sites and a current whole-bunch protocol in CO₂-saturated tanks. Neither the site names nor the cellar method become a regional universal.

featured_connections.reason: The bottle-level proof that Savagnin can be deliberately topped and non-oxidative.
Move from one wine to the grape's wider set of cellar paths.
The domaine's Arbois base opens the legal and geographic layer behind the bottle.

producer:domaine-de-la-tournelle.hero_kicker: Arbois · a cellar decision made legible
producer:domaine-de-la-tournelle.thesis: Évelyne and Pascal Clairet's domaine makes a useful teaching move: Fleur de Savagnin has been a topped expression since the 1990s, so the grape never has to stand in for oxidation.

featured_connections.reason: A recurring Arbois white whose documented composition changes by vintage—a useful check on fixed bottle assumptions.
Follow Château Renard outward to the geographic AOP that classifies it.
Use the documented 2018 bottling as one specific route into Jura Chardonnay.

producer:domaine-de-saint-pierre-jura.hero_kicker: Mathenay · a contemporary estate in motion
producer:domaine-de-saint-pierre-jura.thesis: Fabrice Dodane's Domaine de Saint Pierre adds a contemporary Mathenay perspective: certified organic farming and a recurring Arbois white whose composition needs to be read vintage by vintage.

producer:domaine-de-souch.hero_kicker: Laroin · small scale and patient work
producer:domaine-de-souch.thesis: Domaine de Souch brings the world down to human scale: seven hectares, three local grapes, organic farming, biodynamic principles and manual harvest.

producer:domaine-des-terres-dorees.hero_kicker: Charnay · southern Beaujolais in a live transition

then_now.intro: This is an operating-role transition, not evidence of a sale or retirement.

now.label: NOW · announced transition
now.text: Domaines Roger Zannier holds operation and development, while the announcement keeps Brun involved in a five-year wine-focused transition.

then.label: THEN · before harvest 2024
then.text: The domaine’s public identity centered on Jean-Paul Brun before the new operating arrangement began.

then_now.title: A current producer identity can change without becoming a clean succession myth

producer:domaine-des-terres-dorees.thesis: Terres Dorées holds together southern geography, a source-described Chardonnay area and a 2024 operating transition in which Jean-Paul Brun remains involved. Atlas preserves the source’s unresolved total-acreage arithmetic instead of manufacturing precision.

featured_connections.reason: A cross-appellation estate is a different structure from a single-cru domaine.

producer:domaine-du-tunnel.hero_kicker: Saint-Péray · a later estate built across four appellations
producer:domaine-du-tunnel.thesis: Stéphane Robert created the domaine in 1994 with 2.5 hectares and now works Cornas, Saint-Péray and Saint-Joseph, adding Condrieu in 2013. Its name comes from a rehabilitated railway tunnel at the lieu-dit Barras.

featured_connections.reason: A named site several growers appear in, with no geometry and no single planting date.

producer:domaine-franck-balthazar.hero_kicker: Cornas · one parcel, two planting dates
producer:domaine-franck-balthazar.thesis: Franck Balthazar left a textile factory in 2002, took a Chaillot planting from his uncle Noël Verset, and works older family vines in Mazards and La Côte. One source dates the Chaillot planting to 1912, the other to 1914 — CARTA records both rather than picking.

featured_connections.reason: A grower who returned specifically to plant vines and develop the AOC in the 1980s.
The family's foundational Viognier planting, and the terraces Christine Vernay finished rebuilding.
A variety whose international story begins from an eight-hectare low point.

producer:domaine-georges-vernay.hero_kicker: Condrieu · four generations across a near-disappearance
producer:domaine-georges-vernay.thesis: The Condrieu growers' organisation calls Georges Vernay the man who rebuilt the hillsides and rescued Viognier from obscurity. CARTA carries that leading role and keeps “saved Viognier” as attributed shorthand, because the same recovery contains Francis Vernay's planting, André Perret's 1980s work and Yves Cuilleron's generation.

featured_connections.reason: The historic core is one cluster of a twenty-six-commune appellation, not its definition.

producer:domaine-gonon.thesis: One of the last old-school growers in the appellation's original area around Tournon, Mauves and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, working organically, ploughing the steep slopes by horse, and holding Raymond Trollat's 1915 planting bought on his retirement.

featured_connections.reason: One appellation, two opposite ways of assembling a wine from it.
Neither estate is the appellation, and neither scale is its definition.

producer:domaine-jamet.thesis: The brothers took charge when their father Joseph retired in the mid-1980s and choose each year which of their sites enter the flagship wine. It is the parcel-mosaic answer to the same appellation that also holds a single half-hectare estate.

featured_connections.reason: Sélections Parcellaires since 1989 against a blend rebuilt annually.
Three communes, three producers, three ways of reading the same ground.

producer:domaine-jean-louis-chave.hero_kicker: Hermitage · one wine rebuilt from several sites each year
producer:domaine-jean-louis-chave.thesis: “Bessards is our essential climat; you can't make a Grand Hermitage without it” — and the blend starts from zero every year. A multi-site domaine is one way of organising a hill; named-parcel bottling is another; neither is more traditional than the other.

featured_connections.reason: A Chardonnay route under veil beside a domaine known for topped whites.
A multi-parcel Savagnin route that refuses the single-vineyard assumption.
Chardonnay becomes a site and cellar instrument rather than a generic white-grape card.

producer:domaine-labet.thesis: Domaine Labet is most useful as a parcel-and-process laboratory: topped whites, a documented sous-voile Chardonnay, and a family estate spread across 45 parcels.

featured_connections.reason: Granite slopes and gravel terraces under one legal name.

producer:domaine-laurent-fayolle.hero_kicker: Gervans · northern Crozes-Hermitage is hill country
producer:domaine-laurent-fayolle.thesis: Sixth generation at Gervans, taking control in 2002 when his father and uncle divided the family domaine, farming seven hectares in the granite hills behind the hill of Hermitage. The countercase to reading Crozes-Hermitage as a plain.

producer:domaine-marcel-lapierre.hero_kicker: Morgon · transmission, cellar precision and succession
producer:domaine-marcel-lapierre.thesis: The useful Lapierre story is specific: Marcel’s documented 1981 turn under Jules Chauvet’s guidance, organic certification, current semi-carbonic work, selective sulfur use and a family operation now co-owned by Mathieu and Camille.

featured_connections.reason: A nephew, a Chaillots parcel, and two sources that give its planting date differently.
Early-twentieth-century vines here changed hands within one working lifetime.

producer:domaine-noel-verset.hero_kicker: Cornas · a holding that dispersed rather than passed
producer:domaine-noel-verset.thesis: Divestment from the late 1980s, the largest parcel sold in 2001, wine under his own name until 2006 — and vines that went to Thierry Allemand, to Clape and Courbis, and to his nephew Franck Balthazar. This is what a career ending looks like when nothing is inherited whole.

featured_connections.reason: A leased Chaillot parcel and the use of a cave — neither of them a sale.
An uncle, two shared vintages, and vines rented then purchased.
A sub-cru planted by his grandfather in 1910.

producer:domaine-robert-michel.hero_kicker: Cornas · the hub the transfers run through
producer:domaine-robert-michel.thesis: More than four hundred years of family growing, a father who bottled at the domaine in 1956, a 1975 handover, growth from 1.5 to eight hectares, and a 2006 retirement after which the holding moved in several different ways to several different people.

featured_connections.reason: Rented first, purchased later — the tenure history behind a contemporary producer's geography.

producer:domaine-vincent-paris.hero_kicker: Cornas · family plus work plus a purchase
producer:domaine-vincent-paris.thesis: Robert Michel is Vincent Paris's uncle; Paris made his first two wines with him, inherited most of his vines from his grandfather, and rented and then purchased vines from his uncle including Geynale. Kinship and shared vinification are not mentorship, and CARTA does not add it.

featured_connections.reason: A founder's own domaine stays a separate identity from the project he started with two others.
Part of the expansion generation that followed Condrieu's low point.

producer:domaine-yves-cuilleron.thesis: Taking over a small family domaine in 1987 and building it across six Northern Rhône AOCs plus IGP and Vin de France wines is its own kind of regional history — and the same person co-founded the Seyssuel project.

producer:domaines-landron.hero_kicker: Pays Nantais · farming change with dates
producer:domaines-landron.thesis: Landron's first-party chronology makes a durable Muscadet door: family continuity, a 1987 soil-work turn, organic conversion from 1999 and later biodynamic certification. None becomes a Muscadet rule or an origin myth.

featured_connections.reason: The same legal origin holds a half-hectare estate and a house that buys its neighbours.
Guigal is part of why Condrieu and Viognier became visible to a much larger market.

producer:e-guigal.hero_kicker: Ampuis · scale as part of the real ecology
producer:e-guigal.thesis: Founded in 1946, managed by Marcel Guigal from 1961 when his father lost his sight, with Philippe Guigal as winemaker from 1997 — and a run of acquisitions including Vidal-Fleury, Grippat, de Vallouit and Bonserine plus its own cooperage. A corridor read only through tiny growers would be a false one.

featured_connections.reason: Farming under a source-described lease, with no ownership of parcel or cellar asserted.
The same producer's parcel on the flats in Cornas is bottled as Côtes du Rhône.
Four centuries of Cornas growing, a 1975 handover and a 2006 retirement that dispersed the holding.

producer:guillaume-gilles.hero_kicker: Cornas · four different things passed from one grower to the next
producer:guillaume-gilles.thesis: Robert Michel mentored Gilles, worked with him for six years, leased him a prime Chaillot parcel and made his cave available. Four facts, not one succession. Marcel Juge being his grandfather is a fifth, and it is not evidence that land moved.

producer:jean-foillard.hero_kicker: Villié-Morgon · an individual beyond the shorthand
producer:jean-foillard.thesis: Foillard’s Morgon and Côte du Py associations make a strong place route. The evidence supports Chauvet influence, not an invented formal mentorship, and the map point remains municipality-level orientation rather than vineyard holdings.

featured_connections.reason: A real professional path between two CARTA worlds, unlike the meeting-based transmission stories around it.
The same legal origin holds a no-added-sulfite domaine and a négociant house.

producer:jean-michel-stephan.hero_kicker: Tupin-Semons · a documented route out of Beaujolais
producer:jean-michel-stephan.thesis: Stéphan established his domaine in Côte-Rôtie in 1991 after working at Jean-Paul Brun's Domaine des Terres Dorées, has added no sulfites since 1997, and replants by massale selection of Sérine. Trade sources call the work natural; no self-description was captured, and CARTA records the attribution as attribution.

featured_connections.reason: Named-parcel selection is a way of organising the hill, not a claim that one site is better.

producer:m-chapoutier.thesis: A house dating itself to 1808, with the first Sélections Parcellaires in 1989 and biodynamic cultivation from 1990. A major estate bottling single parcels contradicts the idea that either practice belongs only to small growers.

featured_connections.reason: The current maker's apprenticeship and 2001 handoff turn ‘influence’ into a human chronology.
The earlier chapter: family vines, a 1968 start, and a handoff that kept the elder present.
Leave the cult object behind and return to the grape and its several possible endings.

producer:maison-pierre-overnoy.hero_kicker: Pupillin · a house, people, and a handoff

lenses.text: Most regular cuvées share a front label. Wax color, bottle size and the small bottling date are practical identity clues—not a collecting game.
lenses.title: Read the wax, then read the wine

lenses.text: Extreme US allocation pressure is real and market-specific. It explains why the bottle becomes a status signal; it does not make that bottle necessary for learning the work.
lenses.title: Scarcity can crowd out the lesson

producer:maison-pierre-overnoy.thesis: Read the handoff, not the hype. Pierre Overnoy and Emmanuel Houillon matter as a story of work, transmission and patience before they matter as scarce labels.

featured_connections.reason: Ownership transition is a third structural model beside the family domaine and the parcel selector.

producer:paul-jaboulet-aine.hero_kicker: Tain-l'Hermitage · a house that survived its owners
producer:paul-jaboulet-aine.thesis: Founded on this hill in 1834, creator of Hermitage La Chapelle in 1961, led by Gérard Jaboulet from 1977 until his death in 1997, and passed to the Frey family in 2006 with Caroline Frey in charge. A historic identity outlived a change of owning family.

featured_connections.reason: Twenty-six communes over sixty kilometres, none of which is Arlebosc.
Whole bunches, spontaneous fermentation and about 25 mg/L of sulfur — an importer's description, not a self-description.

producer:romaneaux-destezet.hero_kicker: Arlebosc, Ardèche · with vines in Saint-Joseph
producer:romaneaux-destezet.thesis: The corridor's clearest producer-base-versus-vineyard case. Hervé and Béatrice Souhaut created the estate in 1993 at Arlebosc, in the hills above Saint-Joseph and outside it. A base point here would never be the location of the Saint-Joseph vines.

featured_connections.reason: Verset began divesting in the late 1980s, and Reynard vines went to Allemand.
Working for someone is not being mentored by them, and CARTA keeps the two apart.
Minimal sulfur inside a source-described traditional framework, in a single-variety appellation.

producer:thierry-allemand.hero_kicker: Cornas · worked for everyone, disciple of no one
producer:thierry-allemand.thesis: Day work for Joseph and then Robert Michel, night work helping Noël Verset, and old Reynard vines bought from him. The same importer that records all of it says he is “a disciple of no one's” — which is why CARTA records employment and shared work rather than mentorship.

featured_connections.reason: No cru appellation covers this ground, so quality has nothing to do with the category on the label.
A replanted sector in the same corridor as the crus, and not a delimited wine area.
The founders' own domaines stay separate producer identities from the project they started together.

project:les-vins-de-vienne.hero_kicker: Seyssuel · a frontier, not a ninth cru
project:les-vins-de-vienne.thesis: Three cru producers began replanting the old Seyssuel vineyard north of Vienne in 1996, first vintage 1998, twelve hectares of Syrah and Viognier. The wines are {{term:igp|IGP}} Collines Rhodaniennes. A few kilometres on the map, a total change of legal category.

featured_connections.reason: The project becomes concrete in its Palomino Fino solera wine.
Follow Palomino beyond one project and one regional name.

project:soleras-del-pacifico.hero_kicker: Wine project · a California flor experiment
project:soleras-del-pacifico.thesis: Soleras del Pacífico is a project-shaped subject: a maker, an old Contra Costa planting and a solera practice converging in one wine.

featured_connections.reason: Michel leased a prime parcel here and provided his cave; neither is a transfer of ownership.
A planting acquired from Noël Verset, whose date the two strongest sources give differently.

vineyard:chaillot-cornas.hero_kicker: One name · several growers · no parcel geometry
vineyard:chaillot-cornas.thesis: Chaillot appears in the records of Robert Michel, Noël Verset, Guillaume Gilles and Franck Balthazar. CARTA holds it as a named site with no geometry and does not treat the name as one undivided holding — and it does not turn Michel's lease to Gilles into a sale.

featured_connections.reason: Four generations across a near-disappearance and a rebuilt hillside.
A named site inside a delimited area, with no parcel geometry asserted.

vineyard:coteau-de-vernon-condrieu.thesis: Francis Vernay's foundational hectare of Viognier sits here, and Christine Vernay finished the reconstruction of its terraces. It is the physical continuity behind a recovery usually told as one man's story.

featured_connections.reason: Rented first, purchased later — an asset history that explains a contemporary producer's geography.

vineyard:la-geynale-cornas.hero_kicker: A sub-cru high on the Reynard slope
vineyard:la-geynale-cornas.thesis: Planted by Robert Michel's grandfather in 1910 and worked by Michel until his retirement; vines here were rented and then bought by his nephew Vincent Paris. CARTA records farming and the sourced tenure history, not acquisition of the named site as a whole.

featured_connections.reason: A commune contains a delimited area; it is not the delimited area.
The same producer's Cornas, Côtes du Rhône and Saint-Péray wines make the distinction concrete.

vineyard:les-peyrouses-cornas.hero_kicker: In the commune of Cornas · bottled as Côtes du Rhône
vineyard:les-peyrouses-cornas.thesis: Old-vine Syrah from the flats in the commune of Cornas, sold under a broader appellation. CARTA records the physical locality, the legal designation, and the fact that it does not know where the parcel sits against the delimited boundary — and refuses to close that gap by guessing.

featured_connections.reason: Employment with the Michels, night work with Verset, and a purchase of old vines — three separate records.

vineyard:reynard-cornas.thesis: Robert Michel and Noël Verset both worked Reynard, and Verset sold Thierry Allemand vines here dating to the beginning of the twentieth century. A sale of vines inside a named site is not a sale of the site.

wine:domaine-de-la-tournelle-fleur-de-sa.thesis: One wine that corrects a regional shortcut: 100% Savagnin, grey {{term:marl|marl}}, deliberately {{term:ouille|ouillé}} and non-oxidative.

wine:domaine-labet-chardonnay-du-hasard.hero_kicker: A specific expression · Chardonnay under veil
wine:domaine-labet-chardonnay-du-hasard.thesis: A useful false friend: the grape is Chardonnay, while the most recognizable signal comes from 36–48 months {{term:sous-voile|sous voile}}.

featured_connections.reason: Move from one California solera wine into Palomino's wider naming and place world.
The producer project behind the solera, vineyard choice and flor pathway.

wine:flor-of-evangelho.thesis: The Flor of Evangelho turns an analogy into a bottle: Palomino Fino, an old Contra Costa site, light fortification, fractional blending and ageing under flor.

featured_connections.reason: A valley-long appellation carrying fruit the crus do not cover.
The same producer also makes Cornas and Saint-Péray, which is what makes the contrast legible.

wine:guillaume-gilles-les-peyrouses-roug.hero_kicker: Syrah from Cornas · labelled Côtes du Rhône
wine:guillaume-gilles-les-peyrouses-roug.thesis: The bottle is where the distinction becomes unavoidable. Physical location, commune name and legal designation are three separate facts, and only the third is on the label.

featured_connections.reason: The corridor's legal home for everything the eight crus do not cover.

wine:les-vins-de-vienne-sotanum.thesis: Sotanum is the frontier in one bottle: slopes in the same corridor as the crus, farmed by three cru producers, and a legal category that has nothing to do with either.

featured_connections.reason: Four generations across a near-disappearance, and the terraces rebuilt two generations after the first planting.

wine:vernay-coteau-de-vernon.hero_kicker: Condrieu · the cuvée that survived the low point
wine:vernay-coteau-de-vernon.thesis: The estate's first Coteau de Vernon was released in 1940, from the site where Francis Vernay planted the family's foundational Viognier. It is the continuity behind a recovery usually told as a single biography.

featured_connections.reason: A method, not a quality claim and not a regional identity.

wine:voge-les-bulles-dalain.hero_kicker: 100% Marsanne · brut nature · four years on lattes
wine:voge-les-bulles-dalain.thesis: A {{term:methode-traditionnelle|second fermentation in bottle}} presented by the estate as perpetuating the Saint-Péray tradition that made the region's reputation from the 1830s.

featured_connections.reason: One estate holding the appellation's sparkling tradition and its still departure.

wine:voge-ongrie.thesis: Created when most Saint-Péray came from the traditional method and still wines were vinified in tank. The estate calls Alain Voge the precursor of barrel work here — a precursor inside a tradition, not the inventor of a wine that already existed.
